video_title: Toronto Raptors Full Media Availability | Post Game vs Boston Celtics | November 11, 2026

quotes.speaker: Darko Rajakovic
quotes.summary_phrase: Darko Rajakovic on the team's high turnover rate in the second half
quotes.excerpt: couple of turnovers that should not be happening that for that was a problem in the four quarter
quotes.quote: Through the eight, it is a very high number. In the first quarter, we scored a lot of threes in the first quarter, made 10 of those. I thought we were getting good looks. Down the stretch, a couple of turnovers that should not be happening that for that was a problem in the four quarter. Up to that point, I thought we did a really good job of taking care of the ball. We finished the first half with only three turnovers, but a couple of turnovers, a couple of missed shots, a couple of offensive rebounds that they ended up in their possession, that was the outcome there.
quotes.social_post: Darko Rajakovic on the Raptors second half turnover issues: We finished the first half with only three turnovers, but a couple of turnovers, a couple of missed shots, a couple of offensive rebounds that they ended up in their possession.

structured.context: Darko Rajakovic discusses the team's high turnover rate in the second half against the Boston Celtics.

quotes.speaker: Darko Rajakovic
quotes.summary_phrase: Darko Rajakovic praises Ochai Agbaji's performance against Boston
quotes.excerpt: Ochai Agbaji played a great game tonight with rebounding, with shooting the ball, with energy, with effort
quotes.quote: I thought that Ochai Agbaji played a great game tonight with rebounding, with shooting the ball, with energy, with effort. quotes.speaker: Darko Rajakovic
quotes.summary_phrase: Darko Rajakovic explains the team's process for using challenges
quotes.excerpt: We want to challenge situations that we believe that we can save points
quotes.quote: We have a process in place. We know what we want to challenge. We want to challenge situations that we believe that we can save points, that we can get the possession back. Clippers game was a great example when we had both challenges at the end of the game, used both of those that helped us, and they turned out to be good challenges that they ended up going our way. But those are small things, small possessions that can decide. Obviously, challenges are important, but also you don't want to come in a situation that you're down the stretch, you have a challenge that you did not save points earlier in the game. Points are points, doesn't matter if they happen in the first quarter or in the fourth quarter.
quotes.social_post: Darko Rajakovic on the Raptors challenge process: Points are points, does not matter if they happen in the first quarter or in the fourth quarter.

structured.context: Darko Rajakovic explains the team's internal process and philosophy regarding when to use challenges during a game.

quotes.speaker: Darko Rajakovic
quotes.summary_phrase: Darko Rajakovic on the impact of live-ball turnovers
quotes.excerpt: If it's unforced and you just throw the ball in the hands of a player it's transition
quotes.quote: A lot of them are live-ball turnovers. If it's unforced and you just throw the ball in the hands of a player it's transition. So those are the really hard ones. As I said, first half, we had only three turnovers, which means that we had 12 in the second half, and that's just execution and details and playing through fatigue. Even when you're tired, and right now we're a little bit short-handed with bodies, guys learning how to play through fatigue and still execute in those situations.
quotes.social_post: Darko Rajakovic on the team's fatigue: Right now we are a little bit short-handed with bodies, guys learning how to play through fatigue and still execute in those situations.

structured.context: Darko Rajakovic discusses the impact of live-ball turnovers and the challenge of maintaining execution while playing through fatigue.

quotes.speaker: Allen Graves
quotes.summary_phrase: Allen Graves on his mindset for offensive rebounding
quotes.excerpt: I've always said it I feel like offensive rebounding is just you wanting to do it
quotes.quote: I've always said it I feel like offensive rebounding is just you wanting to do it. I feel like that's the biggest part about it is your mindset about it and I feel like for me, my mindset is go get every every offensive rebound I can. So you know whether that's being physical, trying to get around the guy, whatever it may be, whatever the defense is giving me, just try to make sure I impact the ball, get a hand on it, do something to where we have an extra chance or an extra possession in that case to you know try to score.
quotes.social_post: Jakob Poeltl on his offensive rebounding mindset: I feel like offensive rebounding is just you wanting to do it. My mindset is go get every every offensive rebound I can.

structured.context: Jakob Poeltl explains his personal mindset and approach to offensive rebounding.

quotes.speaker: Allen Graves
quotes.summary_phrase: Allen Graves on maintaining composure despite officiating
quotes.excerpt: I just want to make sure that I'm playing the same no matter what
quotes.quote: I just want to make sure that I'm playing the same no matter what, no matter what anybody's doing. I want to make sure that I'm I'm having the same game. My mindset is not going to change as far as my aggressiveness on defense because that's our Raptors, that's what we build our culture on is on the defensive side of the ball. So making sure that I'm upholding that culture and I'm doing my best whether I'm fouling or whether I'm not, I mean I'm going to play my game.
quotes.social_post: Jakob Poeltl on maintaining composure: My mindset is not going to change as far as my aggressiveness on defense because that is our Raptors, that is what we build our culture on.

quotes.speaker: Ja'Kobe Walter
quotes.summary_phrase: Ja'Kobe Walter on the team's second-half offensive struggles
quotes.excerpt: First quarter we was definitely getting the ball moving more in transition
quotes.quote: First quarter we was definitely getting the ball moving more in transition. We was getting stops and getting out and I think we came out second half, we just didn't start at that same note. We definitely could have just did a better job of getting the ball around, continue to play hard. It started on defense for us too. Defense for us is a lot. When we get stops, we one of the top teams that out and getting transition, so I think we stopped doing that and that kind of affected the way we was playing.

quotes.summary_phrase: Ja'Kobe Walter on the team's mentality after the loss
quotes.excerpt: The blessing about the NBA is you always got another game
quotes.quote: The blessing about the NBA is you always got another game, the next day or the day after that. quotes.summary_phrase: Ja'Kobe Walter on playing through fatigue while short-handed

quotes.speaker: Ja'Kobe Walter
quotes.summary_phrase: Ja'Kobe Walter on the frustration of losing a lead
quotes.excerpt: It's definitely the tough ones where you feel like you beat yourself
quotes.quote: It's definitely the tough ones where you feel like you beat yourself. We don't want to not give them credit, they were hitting shots, they were playing hard as well, but we had a tough we had a we had a lead. We was up what, 20? We had a good lead and at the end of the day we blew the lead. We can't do that, you know. It's tough to we need to figure out how to play with a lead, you know. We can't stop playing the way that we were just because we up. So it's definitely tough to know that we kind of beat ourselves on this one, but we just got to learn from it.
quotes.social_post: Kobe Bufkin on blowing a 20 point lead: We had a good lead and at the end of the day we blew the lead. We can not do that. It is tough to know that we kind of beat ourselves on this one.
